The research order follows the latest EduRank neuroscience table, which ranks thousands of universities using neuroscience publications and citations. EduRank also warns that research rank does not tell you whether a university offers the degree you need, so we verify programme routes separately.

These top neuroscience universities form a strong research shortlist. MIT and Oxford appear later as specialist choices because they can be better than the raw research order for computational neuroscience or postgraduate study.

If you are still choosing a country, compare study routes in the USA, UK study options and Canadian pathways.

2027 application signals already worth knowing

UCL lists its Neuroscience MSci for September 2027 entry with a 13 January 2027 application deadline. UCSF says its Fall 2027 neuroscience PhD application opens on 1 September and closes on 10 November. Oxford is inviting prospective neuroscience students to register for the next 2027 admissions cycle.

Neuroscience University Ranking: How We Chose the List

A neuroscience university ranking should measure neuroscience, not simply the university's overall brand.

We use five filters:

  1. research strength and citation impact;
  2. specialist laboratories and institutes;
  3. undergraduate, master's and PhD availability;
  4. strength in clinical, cognitive, computational and biological neuroscience;

Research.com provides a useful second check because it uses discipline-specific scholar performance rather than the same citation method. Different methodologies produce different orders, which is exactly why one table should not decide your university.

Here's the thing: neuroscience rankings build the shortlist. Programme fit decides the final order.

1. Harvard University

Harvard is the clearest overall answer to “what is the best university for neuroscience?”

Its Program in Neuroscience spans molecular, cellular, systems, computational and cognitive neuroscience. Admitted PiN students receive full tuition and stipend support, health coverage and a relocation allowance. The latest published 12-month stipend package is US$51,500.

2. University College London

UCL is one of the best neuroscience universities for cognitive neuroscience, neuroimaging and clinical brain research.

Its Neuroscience MSci is already published for September 2027 entry. The latest published international tuition signal is £42,700 per year. Applicants should recheck the final fee for their intake.

Best for: Cognitive neuroscience, neuroimaging, MSc/MSci, PhD

3. Johns Hopkins University

Johns Hopkins is one of the top universities for neuroscience when brain science needs a strong medical and biomedical connection.

Its Master's Degree in Neuroscience combines intensive coursework with 12 months of laboratory research across molecular, cellular, systems, cognitive and computational neuroscience.

Best for: Clinical neuroscience, neurobiology of disease, MS, PhD

4. Stanford University

Stanford moves up the shortlist when neuroscience meets technology.

The Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute works across NeuroDiscovery, NeuroHealth and NeuroEngineering. Stanford also supports admitted Neurosciences PhD students with stipend, tuition and health insurance.

For neural devices, the overlap with biomedical engineering is worth comparing.

5. Yale University

Yale is one of the best colleges for neuroscience for students who want biology, cognition and behaviour in one research environment.

Its Department of Neuroscience works from genes and molecules through cells, circuits, behaviour and cognition, with additional strength in disease and translational research.

Best for: Neurobiology, cognition, undergraduate study, PhD

6. University of Toronto

Toronto is one of the strongest neuroscience universities outside the USA and UK.

Its undergraduate routes include cellular/molecular, systems/behavioural and cognitive streams, while the Collaborative Program in Neuroscience connects graduate students across the university.

Best for: Broad neuroscience, cognition, international students

7. University of California, San Francisco

UCSF is a specialist graduate choice. Its Neuroscience Graduate Program is PhD-only and does not offer a standalone master's degree.

All admitted students in good standing receive a stipend plus tuition and fee remission, and international students receive the same financial support.

8. University of Pennsylvania

Penn is one of the best neuroscience PhD programs for interdisciplinary research.

The Neuroscience Graduate Group draws faculty across medicine, arts and sciences, engineering and other schools. Accepted students receive a stipend plus tuition, fees and health-insurance coverage.

Best for: Behavioural neuroscience, interdisciplinary PhD research

9. University of California, Los Angeles

UCLA is one of the strongest best colleges for neuroscience choices for undergraduate students.

Its neuroscience major spans molecular, cellular, systems and behavioural neuroscience, and students can complete research-based capstone work. That combination gives UCLA something a publication ranking alone cannot show: a clear path into hands-on undergraduate research.

Best for: Undergraduate neuroscience, behavioural and systems research

10. University of Michigan

Michigan combines a dedicated undergraduate neuroscience major with a large interdisciplinary doctoral programme.

Its undergraduate route integrates biology, chemistry, quantitative work, biopsychology and laboratory training. The graduate programme includes more than 150 affiliated faculty across behavioural, cognitive, molecular, clinical and computational neuroscience.

Best for: Undergraduate breadth, laboratory training, PhD research

Best Neuroscience Programs by Degree Level

The best neuroscience programs change with the qualification you want. A university can be exceptional for doctoral research and still be the wrong undergraduate choice.

Best Colleges for Neuroscience Undergraduate Students

For the best colleges for neuroscience, prioritise a clear major, early laboratory access, quantitative training and enough electives to specialise later.

Strong options include UCLA, Michigan, Yale, Johns Hopkins, Penn, Toronto and UCL.

That is why the best neuroscience undergraduate programs cannot be selected from publication rankings alone. Research access matters.

How to Choose the Best University for Neuroscience

Start with your field, then your degree level.

If you want brain plus AI, move MIT and Stanford higher. For patient-linked research, prioritise UCSF, Johns Hopkins and UCL. If cognition is the focus, UCL, Yale and Oxford become stronger.

Then check four things:

  • does the university offer the degree you need?
  • can you identify two or three relevant laboratories or supervisors?
  • what will the total cost look like for an international student?

Students on a tighter budget can also explore lower-cost public university routes in Germany, especially when research fit matters more than prestige.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best university for neuroscience in the world?

Harvard is the strongest overall answer based on the latest neuroscience-specific research evidence and the depth of its neuroscience ecosystem. For computational neuroscience, MIT or Stanford may be the better specialist choice.

What are the best universities for neuroscience?

What are the top neuroscience universities?

The top neuroscience universities include Harvard, UCL, Johns Hopkins, Stanford, Yale and Toronto, with UCSF, Penn, UCLA and Michigan completing the current research-led top group.

What are the best neuroscience programs in the world?

The best neuroscience programs in the world include Harvard's PhD, UCL's undergraduate and postgraduate routes, Johns Hopkins' undergraduate, MS and PhD pathways, and funded doctoral routes at Stanford, UCSF and Penn.

What are the best colleges for neuroscience?

The best colleges for neuroscience at undergraduate level include UCLA, Michigan, Yale, Johns Hopkins, Penn, Toronto and UCL. Research access and curriculum matter as much as overall research rank.

What are the best neuroscience undergraduate programs?

UCLA, Michigan, Yale, Johns Hopkins, Penn, Toronto and UCL are strong best neuroscience undergraduate programs candidates. Prioritise laboratory access, quantitative training and course flexibility.

What are the best neuroscience PhD programs?

Which country is best to study neuroscience?

The USA has the deepest concentration of major neuroscience research universities and funded PhD routes. The UK is strong for focused master's study and cognitive or clinical neuroscience, while Canada offers strong research universities and broad international study pathways.

Which Neuroscience University Should You Choose for 2027?

The best neuroscience universities in the world give you more than a famous name. They give you access to the right laboratories, methods, supervisors and research community.

Harvard is the strongest all-round research choice. UCL offers unusual breadth across undergraduate and postgraduate neuroscience. Johns Hopkins is excellent for medically connected research. Stanford and MIT stand out when neuroscience meets technology. UCSF and Penn become especially attractive for funded doctoral study.

The smartest question is not simply “Which university ranks highest?”

It is “Which of the best universities for neuroscience fits the work I want to do in 2027?”
